chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rib'i from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them) used to command the children to combine the Maghrib and the later Isha prayers, and he would say, 'It is better for them than to sleep through it.'

key_terms.عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَام: Peace be upon them (used for the Imams and their father)

ai.seo_question: How should parents teach young children to perform the Maghrib and Isha prayers according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Sajjad (AS) highlights the pedagogical approach of early prayer training, emphasizing consistency over rigid timing to prevent children from missing the obligation entirely due to sleep. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of gradual habituation, where the priority is establishing the connection with Salah before enforcing strict adherence to individual prayer times.
